Prologue

The setup, as Moon Studios describes it. Only what the studio’s own announcement and the game’s text state is listed here.

A thousand years ago

The first Pestilence

The Pestilence is an unholy plague that corrupts and destroys everything it touches. It had not been seen for a thousand years before it returned.

Who you are

The Cerim

You are a Cerim — a member of a group of mystical holy warriors, imbued with remarkable powers and sworn to defeat the Pestilence at any cost. The game’s own gear text calls their cloaks and gloves “imbued with the words of the Sayer.”

841 TE

The King is dead

The year is 841, and King Harol is dead. The crown passes to his son, Magnus — and the Pestilence has returned.

The Church

Madrigal Seline

Madrigal Seline, a ruthlessly ambitious figure in the Church, sees the Pestilence as a chance to prove herself in the eyes of her god.

Where it is happening

Isola Sacra

The Cerim is sent to Isola Sacra, a struggling island of crumbling ruins where the Pestilence has transformed the locals, and is drawn into the conflict between the island’s rulers and the rebels who seek to overthrow them.

The reveal itself

The October 2nd post is art, not design. Moon published five renders with one line of copy between them: shocked steel, walking fortresses, plague harnessing, frozen majesty and gilded skulkers. Those five phrases sit in the same order as the five images, which is how this dossier pairs them. Confirmed

No class in the post carries a stat line, a weapon list, a trait, or a number of any kind. The studio closed by pointing at the next Wicked Inside for the class system deep dive.

How the system is changing

Each weapon archetype maps to a class. Using a weapon earns points that unlock that class's traits, you equip six at a time, and mastering a weapon lets you extract its runes. Classes also get a super on a charge bar. Reported

Two changes matter more than the rest: weapons lose their attribute requirements, and 1.0 arrives with a save wipe. The first turns attributes from gates into pure scaling and survivability decisions. The second means nothing you build before launch carries over.

Factions & Classes

House of the Born God

Cleric

Support-focused holy warriors who heal allies and smite foes with divine magic.

Crusader

A divine warrior wielding massive greathammers to smite evil.

Monk

Martial artist mixing stamina and focus for powerful spiritual strikes.

Paladin

Holy hammer fighter/guardian.

The Hunter's Guild

Archer

Ranged fighters wielding bows to strike enemies from a distance.

Barbarian

Ferocious warriors with raw physicality, wielding huge clubs to smash through enemy lines.

Berserker

Dominant warriors wielding massive greataxes for devastating sweeps. Wades directly into combat and stays there. Benefits from staying in combat and trading blows with enemies.

Marauder

A warrior type class that focuses on in-your-face combos. Trading blows is a plus as it increases damage capabilities. No nonsense axe combos.

The Sacrament Guard

Lithe spearmen harnessing faith-based leaps to pierce defenses.

Guardian

Balanced fighters wielding straight swords, equally adept with Strength and Dexterity.

Scuttlers

A cold-themed mage who freezes, chills, and shatters enemies.

Rules That Govern

Commit to one element

An elemental gem grants no enchantment power if another elemental gem is already equipped anywhere on your gear. Mixing plague, lightning, fire and ice does not diversify a build, it disables most of it. Pick the element the class is named after and run it alone.

Sockets follow rarity

Common gear carries four gem slots; magical, plagued and unique carry one each. Plagued items add four upside slots and one mandatory downside. A fully socketed common piece is often stronger than a rare one.

One enchantment per group

Magical and plagued enchantments belong to groups, and an item cannot carry two from the same group. Miscellaneous is the exception. Plan an item's rolls as a set, not a wishlist.

Exalting caps at four

Each exalt lifts one roll by 25% and can push past the normal maximum. In the game the Watcher picks which enchantment gets it at random; the builder lets you choose, so you can plan a result. Four is the ceiling per item, and the Watcher's material cost climbs steeply — the fourth needs two each of Torn Sinew, Torn Marrow and Torn Husk.

Runes are category-locked

Every weapon has four rune slots, and a rune only fits weapons in its own category. Extracting a rune to move it destroys the weapon it came from. Unique weapons cannot be changed at all.

Facets are always a trade

A facet is one roll per item, fixed at the drop, and every one of them gives with one hand and takes with the other — Heavy is +20% damage for +25% stamina cost, Mystic is Focus Gain for stamina regen. Pick the facet whose cost lands on a stat the class does not use. Reported

Resistance facets scale with armor

Fireproof, Frostwoven, Insulated and Purified add an armor value toward one element rather than a flat percentage, and the value grows with your total armor — roughly 70–80 at 125 armor, far less below it. On a light-armor class they do little. Reported

Upgrades tier at 4 and 8

Gear runs from level 1 to 16, with tier breaks at 4 and 8. Higher-level items are likelier to roll facets but demand more from your attributes or character level.

What to watch next

The Wicked Inside showcase carries the full class system deep dive, and the December beta puts all twenty-four classes in players' hands. Those two events will replace most of the projected sections above.

Three things to check the moment numbers appear: whether the freeze and shatter from the experimental build survived into 1.0 and how it reads in the gear rules, what Cutthroat and Harbinger actually are, and how class traits interact with gems and enchantments — if traits can supply an element, the mono-element rule changes shape entirely.

Infusions

Heads up: gem infusions will be introduced into the game at the 1.0 launch, allowing you to combine gems to create new and unique traits.

Infusions are the gems. Every one of them socketed into a weapon, a shield or a piece of armor, and what it does depends on where it sits: the same stone reads differently on a blade than on a helmet. There are forty-two in the live game, in twenty-one families of two tiers each — the chipped, tiny and small stones are tier one, the mottled and medium stones tier two.

Sockets are the constraint. Common gear carries four, magical, plagued and unique gear carry one, so a fully socketed common piece can out-build a rare one. The elemental gems carry a second constraint of their own, set out under that heading below.

Each family is listed once with both tiers side by side, grouped by what the gem is for. Item value is the merchant price in bronze. Effects are given per slot exactly as the game states them; where every armor piece reads the same the row is collapsed to All armor.

The whole list is read from the game’s own files, so it tracks the live build. The class system arriving at 1.0 may rework what these stones do; the loadout tables in the class profiles above already assume the current values.

Elemental

One element per build. The weapon gem grants the infusion; the shield gem deals that element while blocking; on armor every piece gives Enchantment Power, but only if it is the sole elemental gem you wear.

Enchantments

Enchantments are the rolls on magical and plagued gear. Every one is a range — the number an item actually carries lands somewhere inside it, and exalting at the Watcher pushes it up by a quarter per step, four steps at most. There are 405 of them in the live game across seven kinds of item.

They come in three pools. Magical is the ordinary pool. Plagued is the stronger pool that plagued gear rolls from, and plagued gear always carries one Downside alongside its upsides. An item never carries two enchantments from the same group, Misc excepted, so a piece's rolls read as a set rather than a list.

The pools are sorted here by the piece they land on, because that is how you meet them: standing over a drop, deciding whether the gloves are worth the sockets. Within each piece the magical and plagued pools are grouped the way the game groups them, which is also the rule for what can share an item.

Bows are listed separately from weapons; they share most of the melee pool and add their own dodge-and-retaliate rolls. Where a class profile above names an enchantment, it is one of these.

Blink, Channel, Cold Enchantment, Cold Resistance, Damage Surge, Electric Enchantment, Electric Resistance, Focus Halo, Heal, Heal Aura, Heat Enchantment, Heat Resistance, Illuminate, Plague Enchantment, Plague Resistance, Poise Shield, Pulse of Health, Repair, Return, Scream, Stamina Wellspring, Thorns

Enchants and infuses your gear in Sacrament. Her stall sells magic weapons and utility runes, and the stock grows with each shop level. She's friendly to Cerim.

Services

Enchant1 per itemEnchants an item, raising the item's rarity to either Rare (blue) or Plagued (purple) and granting it additional and potentially powerful affixes at random. This process also removes the last 3 Gem slots and 2 Rune slots from the enchanted item.
Infuse1 per gemInfuses the power of a Gem into the chosen item, granting additional passive effects while that item is equipped. Infusion requires 1 free Gem slot on the target item.
Runeno chargeAdds a Rune to a weapon or allows a Rune to be extracted from a weapon. Note that extracting a Rune destroys the item it is removed from and existing runes cannot be overwritten.

Cerim Crucible

The Seneschal keeps the Crucible and is paid in Gloamseed rather than coin.

Crucible keeper

The Seneschal

OfferingsCrucible Atrium

Within the Crucible Atrium

Keeps the Cerim Crucible. Gloamseed buys Offerings that unlock Crucible features one at a time. Once you buy Scavenged Remains the Seneschal also sells 40 random picks from weapons, armor, runes, embers, gems and rings.
